tasks.title: Pick a cube off a table
tasks.desc: Scripted closed-loop expert: IK to above the cube, descend, close the rack-and-pinion gripper, lift. This expert gets 97% over 100 random placements.
tasks.result: Cube lifted 126 mm, held by both pads.

tasks.title: Pick by the learned policy
tasks.desc: A neural network trained by behaviour cloning on the expert's demos (MLP on joint state, cube and touch). No IK and no script: it outputs the 8 actions every 40 ms.
tasks.result: 13/20 picks on cube positions it never saw in training.

tasks.title: Pick from the floor
tasks.desc: Lift all the way down, head tilted to the floor, right hand to a cube 0.38 m from the base centre, just past the front of the base.
tasks.result: Cube lifted 199 mm off the floor.

tasks.title: Reach up to a 1.5 m shelf
tasks.desc: The stepper raises the torso the full 650 mm at its real 25 mm/s. The right arm folds up close to the body, then reaches to the shelf.
tasks.result: Hand at 1.46 m, 0 cm past the shelf's front edge. The lift took 26 s.

tasks.title: Hold 0.5 kg in each hand, arms straight out
tasks.desc: The worst gravity load for the shoulders and elbows. The blue blocks are the 0.5 kg payloads.
tasks.result: Worst joint sag 2.1°. Shoulder pitch at 5.9 N·m of its 20.8 N·m peak.

tasks.title: Drive, turn, and stop hard
tasks.desc: Torso part way up. 0.6 m/s forward, a turn, then a 3 m/s² stop: harder than the base controller allows.

tasks.title: Shove at the head, worst pose
tasks.desc: Torso at the top, arms forward. A 25 N push at the head for 1.5 s. The check finds the tipping point at about 30 N.

tasks.title: Wave
tasks.desc: Shoulder roll up, then upper-arm yaw and wrist roll back and forth.
